I am ready to play Monopoly.

I have $619 and am on ILLINOIS_AVENUE after paying rent to p3. My holdings include a yellow monopoly with one house on Ventnor and Marvin Gardens, plus unmortgaged properties like Atlantic Avenue and Park Place.

p1 is bankrupt. p2 has $512 and no monopolies. p3 has $3,528 and two jail turns. He owns a light blue monopoly with hotels on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut.

p3 also owns four railroads and the green properties States, Illinois, and Pennsylvania Avenue. The bank has 30 houses and 9 hotels remaining. I will not build this turn because it would drop my cash below the hotel cover threshold. On my next roll from Illinois, I could land on B&O Railroad for $200.

Rolling from Illinois leads to several destinations. I own Atlantic Avenue, Ventnor Avenue, and Marvin Gardens. Water Works is owned by p2, so landing there would cost up to $120. Pacific belongs to p2 with no monopoly, meaning standard rent applies. North Carolina is unowned. The biggest threats are B&O Railroad and Short Line, both costing $200.

The $200 railroad rent is easily covered by my $619 cash. I will not hit the light blue hotels this turn because I must go around the board first. I am now weighing whether to build on Atlantic Avenue, which would cost $220 for one house.

I will build one house on Atlantic Avenue to match my other yellow properties. This costs $150 and leaves me with $469. Rent on Atlantic rises from $44 to $110.

p2 would need a 12 to land on Atlantic from Virginia. p3 is in jail with two turns already served and is now attempting a third roll.

p3 cannot reach Atlantic Avenue from jail in one roll. The distance is 16 spaces, which exceeds the maximum of 12. p2 also cannot land on Ventnor or Marvin from Virginia in a single roll. Only p2 rolling a 12 to reach Atlantic remains a realistic threat.

The expected value of building on Atlantic is negligible. The $150 cost only yields a 1/36 chance of an extra $66 in rent. I will not build this turn.

I cannot reach GO from Illinois in one roll. I would land on Short Line instead. The light blue hotels are at the start of the board, so I must go around first. If I land on Go to Jail, I will be safe from those hotels for a while.

A roll of 12 lands on Short Line for $200. From there, an 11-space roll could reach Oriental for $600. Building Atlantic would leave only $269 after that hit. I need to keep roughly $600 cash before entering the light blue danger zone.

I mapped the exact sequence from Illinois. Rolling 2 lands on B&O Railroad for $200. Rolling 3 lands on Atlantic Avenue. Rolling 4 lands on Ventnor Avenue. Rolling 5 lands on Water Works, costing only $50 because p2 owns both utilities. Rolling 6 lands on Marvin Gardens. Rolling 7 lands on Go to Jail.

Rolling 9 from Illinois lands on North Carolina, an unowned green property priced at $300. I can afford to buy it.

I will buy North Carolina. It is a trade chip that blocks p3 from completing his green monopoly and prevents p2 from acquiring Pacific cheaply.

The $600 cash rule is for paying light blue hotels without selling houses. Post-build cash would be $469, which does not clear that threshold. Mortgageable holdings total $305.

Cash plus mortgageable holdings totals $924, comfortably above the $600 hotel threshold. Building one house on Atlantic would leave $774, still above that mark. The earlier $200 rule applied to a second-house tier.

I will not build on Atlantic this turn. Post-build cash would drop to $469, below the $600 threshold. The light blue hotels are still far away from my current position on Illinois Avenue. I will wait until after p2 and p3 finish their turns and I roll again.

I will not buy North Carolina now. The action state does not include a buy option, and I can decide later if I land there.

I am reconsidering the $150 house on Atlantic. p2 is on Virginia and can only reach Atlantic with a roll of 12.

I realized I must build before p2's turn so the rent applies. If I build now and end my turn, p2 rolling a 5 from Virginia would land on New York Avenue. I own all three orange properties, but St James and Tennessee are mortgaged, so no rent is collected there.

Standard Monopoly rules confirm that a color group cannot collect doubled rent while any property in it is mortgaged. Because St James and Tennessee are mortgaged, New York Avenue would only pay base rent. I also cannot build houses on the orange set until all three properties are unmortgaged.

Unmortgaging both orange properties would cost $198. That money is better spent on the yellow houses already in place. p2 can land on New York Avenue for only $16 base rent, so unmortgaging is not worthwhile.

Atlantic's one-house rent is $110, a $66 increase over the base $44. Yellow is a frequent landing spot for players coming out of jail. The liquidity constraint remains the main issue. p3's hotels are the primary threat. I am weighing whether to build high enough on yellow to bankrupt p2 or survive p3's hotels.

p3 can reach Atlantic Avenue from jail in two rolls. After leaving jail on spaces 12 through 22, a roll of 5 or 4 lands them on Atlantic. This makes the one-house rent jump to $110 worthwhile.

The turn sequence confirms p3 cannot reach yellow on the same turn they leave jail. After my next roll from Illinois, I will have another post-turn decision before p3 can land on yellow.

I will not build on Atlantic now. The missed rent from p2 is too small to justify the $150 liquidity risk.

I am now considering a trade with p2 or p3. I own both dark blue properties, but Boardwalk is mortgaged and cannot be developed until unmortgaged. Unmortgaging it would cost $220, leaving me with $399.

Unmortgaging Boardwalk would leave only $399, which is too little to build evenly on dark blue. Unmortgaging the orange properties would leave $421 after paying $198, but that money is better spent on yellow houses to protect against hotel hits.

I will not trade Mediterranean Avenue to p3, since that would let them complete the brown monopoly and hotel it. p2 has two jail cards, but p3 is about to leave jail anyway, so those cards are not a useful trade chip.

Jail cards are less useful now that p3 is leaving jail. Staying in jail late game could avoid hotel hits, but p2 will not trade cheaply for them. I cannot offer p2 a monopoly since I lack the missing pieces. p3 might want Mediterranean Avenue to complete the brown set, though I would need to give up both dark blue properties to let them finish the dark blue set.

p3 cannot complete the orange set, so they would not trade for it. A brown hotel at $250 is less threatening than light blue hotels at $550–600, but giving p3 another hotel strip is too risky. I would lose Mediterranean Avenue as a mortgage buffer and property. p3 has no incentive to trade away their assets. I am now exploring whether a trade with p2 could hurt p3.

I will end my turn. Buying Pacific would not block p3 from completing green, since North Carolina is unowned and the rent is too low to justify spending cash.
